[[File:Cairienmap.png|thumb|An overhead map shows the Cairhienin love for straight lines.]][[File:Topless Towers.jpg|thumb|right|The Topless Towers over the city of Cairhien.]]

'''Cairhien''' is the capital of the [[Cairhien|kingdom of the same name]]. A large, square-shaped city, it is located on the banks of the [[River Alguenya]] just south of its junction with the [[Gaelin]]. The city is known primarily as the seat of the king [[Galldrian]], for the institution of the political game [[The Great Hunt/Chapter 30|''Daes Dae'mar'']], and for a hatred above all else of the [[Aiel]] since the [[Aiel War]]. It was once known as Al’cair’rahienallen and was originally built by [[Ogier]].{{ref/book|6|20}}

== Gates of the City==
The north gate of the city is known as the [[Jangai Pass|Jangai]] Gate and the east gate of the city is known as the Dragonwall Gate.{{ref/book|6|25}} Much of the poorer citizens live outside the gates in small gate towns. The area before the walls is called the [[Foregate]]. This area is inhabited by what the soldiers describe disparagingly as "peasants." These were former farmers who left their farms at the [[Spine of the World]] during the [[Aiel War]] never to return.{{ref/book|2|25}} In order to keep these "peasants" appeased, the king, [[Galldrian]], hires [[Gleeman|gleemen]], displays fireworks and performs entertainments at his expense. [[Loial]] finds this distasteful. The city is known for its class distinctions due to ''Daes Dae'mar'' which forces people to choose which noble houses they adhere to and ally with.

==Parallels==
[[File:1024px-Medieval Bologna.jpg|alt=City of medieval Bologne with a hundred towers of great height contained within a city wall.|thumb|Artist's impression of Bologne, one of the inspirations for the city of Cairhien's Topless Towers.]]The city of Cairhien may be based on Caerleon, an important city in Arthurian lore. Many of its architectural features, such as the topless towers, are reminiscent of medieval Bologna (Italy), which had more than 180 towers of up to 100m tall.{{ref|[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Towers_of_Bologna Towers of Bologna]}}
